A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and the added Appendix H.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original lemma-generation experiments, comparisons across GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Pro, and a reflection ablation. Table 2 reports the system's iterative results.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original lemma-quality, backbone, and reflection-ablation experiments, alongside the iterative results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The documented monotonicity procedure receives limited corrections: Algorithm 2 checks distinct rather than adjacent terminal pairs, and Appendix F.3.1 restricts implicit-point monotonicity checks to baseline verification functions. The core lemma-generation, verification, and reflection pipeline remains intact.

E1.justification: Both versions address the same Steiner-ratio task and verify the same four geometric cases, distinguished by D's topology and the range of f. Appendix H introduces no additional evaluated task or scenario.

E2.justification: The historical lower-bound comparisons and the reflection-disabled comparator are retained. No competing method is added or removed from the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The four-case verification design, representative Case 2, GPT-5/Gemini 3 Pro configurations, approximately 100 experimental rounds, and ten-round reflection ablation remain unchanged. The added explanation of lemma effectiveness clarifies an existing measurement rather than establishing a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The backbone robustness experiments, reflection ablation, and observations about boundary dominance and topological degeneracy are retained. No additional ablation, robustness test, or empirical supplementary analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Round and iteration reporting remains unchanged. Neither version reports seed-level replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The backbone-robustness paragraph revises its approximate convergence value from 0.855 to 0.8559. Figure 9 and Table 2 retain the same nine-step trajectory from 0.8282 to 0.8559, and the lemma-quality and ablation findings remain unchanged. This limited numerical revision does not establish a new performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 corrects the pruning-length equalities to inequalities. Proposition 37 refines the relocated Algorithm 2 correctness proof with explicit applicability conditions and derivative cases, while Appendix D.2 adds reasoning about monotonicity after substituting f=d. Most mathematics in Appendix H restates existing results.

C1.justification: The central contribution and certified 0.8559 bound remain unchanged. The later conclusion additionally identifies two transferable design principles and claims applicability to other settings with exact verification and localizable failures.

C2.justification: The new limitations section discusses CAD scalability, barriers to larger Steiner topologies, and human verification as a limit on autonomy. The conclusion also specifies conditions for transferring the framework. These extend the implications of computational restrictions and manual checking already disclosed in v1.

D1.justification: Table 3 supplies more precise edge-specific parameter dependencies, and Appendix F.4 explains split enumeration, including handling self-loops and parallel edges during contraction. The later version also defines lemma effectiveness more explicitly and adds a specific certificate-implementation link in Appendix H.5.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is largely retained after relocation. A limited substantive citation change replaces the Jumper et al. (2020) AlphaFold 2 entry with Senior et al. (2020), and attribution of the induction framework and baseline lemmas becomes more explicit. Most other reference changes update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Related work moves from the main text to Appendix A, the experimental and proof appendices are reordered, and the conclusion and limitations discussion expand. Appendix H creates a substantial separate exposition for mathematicians, materially changing the document's organization and available reading routes.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, clarifies Figure 4's caption, revises Figure 9's comparison labels, and redisplays several existing figures in Appendix H. The principal diagrams, chart structure, and iterative-results table are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical clarity through corrected pruning inequalities and a more explicit monotonicity proof, and improves transparency through concrete limitations and certificate-access information. Appendix H makes the existing argument easier to follow independently of the LLM narrative. These are useful but limited gains; the central bound and experimental evidence remain essentially unchanged.
